items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: Al Morgan used to be bass player with Cab Calloway, so he had quit Cab Calloway here, and we became very good friends

ctx.x: See, Cozy was a rudimental drummer, you know, and so he was a stickler for rudiments. And I think that basically, he really did help me because I'm not sure if I would have been as good as reading if I had not spent hours and hours with Cozy, because that's all we would do - just stay in the book, stay in the book. All day. And we must have gone through

3 or 4 books while he was here. Then after they left then Fats Waller came out, and Al Morgan was here at the time. Al Morgan used to be bass player with Cab Calloway, so he had quit Cab Calloway here, and we became very good friends, and so he knew Fats from New York, and so Fats was looking for a drummer, and so the three of us were the Fats Waller trio at the Famous Door, you know.
What was it like working with Fats?
